newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU IS MANHANDLED BUT HANGS ON FOR WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU IS MANHANDLED BUT HANGS ON FOR WIN.

text.p: Highly-touted Japanase pitcher Hideki Irabu was tagged for five runs and nine hits in five innings, but he managed to hang on long enough behind the Yankees' big bats to win his second straight major league victory on Tuesday.
Tino Martinez's three-run homer capped a six-run third inning and the New York Yankees pounded out a 12-6 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
Irabu walked one, struck out four and also balked.
Ramiro Mendoza gave up one run and four hits over the final four innings to earn his first major-league save.

Martinez tied a career-best when his belted his 31st homer of the season into the right-field seats, giving the Yankees a 7-1 bulge. Martinez also hit 31 homers in 1995 as a member of the Seattle Mariners.

New York banged out seven consecutive hits as they batted around in the third inning. The Yankees also batted around in the eighth -- the third time they batted around twice in the same game this season, and have batted around 25 times this season.
Every New York starter had as least one hit and eight scored a run.
Charles Nagy (9-6), was reached for eight runs and nine hits over 2 1/3 innings. In his two starts against the Yankees this season, Nagy has yielded 13 runs and 15 hits, lasting just four innings.
New York pitchers surrendered more than three runs for the first time in 13 games.
